data.title: Zone File Daily Diff Anomaly Detection
data.description: Detects anomalous patterns in daily zone file diffs: unusual volume of new registrations in a single TLD, concentration of registrations at specific registrars, or patterns suggesting algorithmic generation including lexical similarity, sequential naming, and entropy clustering. Zone file diffs provide a ground-truth view of new domain registrations across gTLDs and many ccTLDs. Fraudulent campaigns using RDGA, TDS, or AI-generated domain strategies produce detectable statistical anomalies in daily diff data — particularly registrar concentration spikes, abnormal per-TLD registration volumes, and clusters of domains with similar character distribution or word structure. This rule establishes rolling baselines for registrar-TLD combinations and alerts when daily new registration counts exceed three standard deviations from the 30-day rolling mean, or when entropy analysis reveals clustering indicative of algorithmic or template-based domain generation.

enrichment_required.source: Statistical baseline enrichment (z-score against 30-day rolling mean)

falsepositives: Promotional pricing events by registrars that cause legitimate registration spikes
New TLD launches or sunrise periods with high legitimate registration volume
Large enterprise domain portfolio acquisitions through a single registrar
